applicable_when: The kernel consumes 255 registers/thread (the absolute PTX maximum), hard-limiting occupancy to 12.5% (Block Limit Registers=2 blocks/SM). This causes severe scheduler starvation (58.4% idle cycles, only 1.96 active warps/scheduler vs 16 max) and forces register spilling to local memory (confirmed by MemoryCacheAccessPattern flagging uncoalesced local loads/stores at 56.34% speedup). The current BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=128 accumulator alone requires 16384 FP32 values — far exceeding 255 registers — so the compiler spills heavily. Reducing tile sizes via @triton.autotune will cut register usage, raise occupancy, eliminate spilling, and fix the partial-wave tail.
